ON THIS DEVICE

Manage songs

Your audio and charts stay in this browser. Export a backup to move a song to another device or protect it from cleared browser storage.

Game version 39
YOUR NOTES. YOUR ARRANGEMENT.

Chart files

Import a .chart file from Moonscraper or another chart editor, with its matching audio. Guitar, Bass and Drums are supported.

Positive values move notes later in the audio. Tempo changes and the chart’s own offset are included.

Choose a chart to see its instruments, difficulties and note counts.

Supplied non-empty difficulties replace those levels for the matching audio. Other saved levels and instruments stay as they are. For a new part, missing levels are derived from the most detailed supplied chart.

Fretted notes, chords, holds and individual drum hits are supported. Open frets, sustained drum rolls, vocals, MIDI and six-fret charts are not imported. HOPO/tap, accent and phrase markings use Riffbound’s normal gameplay.

Export the open song

Export notes for editing. Keep the matching audio beside the chart; use Manage songs for a complete .riffpack backup.
REPEAT. IMPROVE.

Practice a section

Loop a fill or solo. Practice does not change your best score.

Slower playback also lowers the audio pitch. Highway speed changes note spacing without changing the song.
MATCH YOUR DEVICE

Timing calibration

Use the speakers or headphones you play with. Listen to the clicks, then tap in time with them. Keep tapping for the whole test.

Twelve beats. The first two help you settle into the rhythm.

Positive values give your taps more time; negative values move the hit window earlier. This adjusts playback timing, not which drum a color represents.
TAKE THE STAGE WITH YOU

Install & play offline

Game updates download automatically while online and apply when you are between songs with your work saved. Open a saved In Bloom drum track to receive its latest Expert and Hard corrections. Songs stay on this device and can be opened offline.

On iPhone, open this link in Safari, then Share → Add to Home Screen. On Android, use your browser’s Install or Add to Home Screen option.

Keep a .riffpack backup of songs you want to keep. Clearing browser data removes local songs and the offline copy.
SOUNDCHECK

Find your rhythm.

Colored notes travel down the highway. Play them when they reach the glowing fret line near the bottom.

Choose Guitar, Drums, Bass or Vocals beside the chart before starting a track.

  1. Auto-chart your songChoose Guitar, Drums, Bass or Vocals above the upload button, then upload a full song or isolated track. Whole song builds all four charts; Separate parts builds the parts you check. Each part has its own preview and highway; the original song plays in every mode. Changing instruments rebuilds the song separately. Pick Easy, Medium, Hard or Expert, then choose Preview chart to watch the notes play automatically. Move Preview from to hear another part. Choose Play track or Play yourself when you are ready.
  2. Tap fretsPress D F J K L for green, red, yellow, blue, and orange. On a phone, tap the colored fret buttons.
  3. Hold + strumHold the matching fret keys, then press Enter at the right moment. Hold all the matching frets for chords.
  4. Play a vocal melodyVocal pitch runs from low to high across the five colors. Tap D F J K L or the matching pads and hold long notes. This mode charts the melody for pad play; it does not use your microphone or recognize lyrics. Other pitched instruments in a full recording can affect the estimate.
  5. Keep it ringingHold a fret through a long note's tail for extra points. Build a streak to reach a 4× multiplier.
  6. Play the drumsThe drum lanes run left to right: D — red snare, F — yellow closed/open hi-hat, J — blue tom, K — orange cymbal, and L — green floor tom. The green pad / L also hits orange cymbal notes; one green hit covers orange and green notes arriving together. Press Space or Enter for wide purple kick bars. Alternate both keys for fast kicks, or use the wide touch pedal. Play other simultaneous notes together. On a phone, tap the matching ring or the kick pedal.
  7. Unleash OverdriveAt 50% charge, press Shift on drums, Space on Guitar, Bass or Vocals, or the Overdrive button to double your multiplier. Escape pauses the track.

Easy uses fewer notes and simpler rhythms; Medium adds more notes; Hard adds denser fills and chords; Expert keeps every distinct detected note from the audio; Hard, Medium and Easy are reduced from that full chart. Rebuild an existing song’s instrument chart to apply updated audio charting. Guitar and Bass use three frets on Easy, four on Medium, and five on Hard/Expert. Drum colors always represent the same drums. Vocal melody keeps its five pitch colors. Space or Enter plays the drum kick; Shift activates drum Overdrive. This is free play: missed notes lower crowd energy, but the song keeps going. The built-in track uses original synthesized music. Uploaded charts estimate instrument parts from the mixed audio; they are not exact transcriptions.
